historical_references.reference: Deenabandhu was a prominent Bengali Hindu leader and poet who was an active participant in the Indian freedom struggle. He was born in 1896 in the village of Kantal in Birbhum, West Bengal. He joined the Indian National Congress in 1920 and became a prominent figure in the non-cooperation movement led by Mahatma Gandhi. He was arrested several times for his involvement in the freedom struggle. After India's independence, he served as a Member of Parliament from West Bengal.

Deenabandhu Mukherjee was a noted Bengali poet, writer, and social reformer. He was born in 1896 in the village of Kantal in Birbhum, West Bengal. He was deeply influenced by the works of Rabindranath Tagore and Kazi Nazrul Islam. He wrote poetry that reflected the social and political realities of his time, often focusing on the plight of the common man. His most famous works include 'Hariprasad Chhaterjee', 'Banglar Mati', and 'Deenabandhu Samajpatra'.
